entities.summary: Leopold August Abel was a German violinist and composer. He was born in Köthen in 1718. He was the elder brother of Karl Friedrich Abel, and the grandfather of Johann Leopold Abel. August Abel studied violin under Benda. He played in the orchestra of the theatre at Brunswick, and was successively conductor of the court band to the Prince of Schwarzburg-Sondershausen (1758), the Margrave of Schwedt (1766), and the Duke of Schwerin (1770). He composed a sinfonia a 8 voci in 1766, and some of his violin studies and other compositions are in the possession of the Gesellschaft der Musikfreunde at Vienna.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Leopold August Abel was a prominent violinist and composer in Western Europe during the Early Modern era. His compositions were performed by notable orchestras, including the court band to the Prince of Schwarzburg-Sondershausen, demonstrating his regional influence.
